title: Enjoy a chosen pleasure within a flexible boundary

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Temperance governs a good without making pleasure shameful. Across entertainment, spending, comfort and status, ask what purpose the activity serves and what it displaces. Food and sexual life involve nourishment, health, consent and personal circumstances; restriction, deprivation or enduring unwanted contact are not practice goals.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Kai has 30 free minutes for a familiar word game, then an agreed call. The game is free and can pause at any turn. Kai chooses a 25-minute window plus 5 minutes to prepare. A cosmetic upgrade costs 12 discretionary units but changes no play feature; Kai’s optional budget is 10. No purchase or restriction of essentials is required.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Choose a stop/exception rule, then compare the time and purchase decisions. Name how you would carry the same purpose check to another optional pleasure without transferring an unsafe method.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person is offered an expensive badge that confers no access or skill and exceeds their discretionary budget. Must rejecting all recognition become the new goal?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Stop by 25 minutes to prepare; no game condition supplied justifies missing the call. The12-unit cosmetic purchase exceeds 10 and is optional. Later fiction: Kai stops at 27, still makes the call, and declines the purchase; the personal window overran even though the duty was met. Partial: hide the overrun. Incorrect: withhold food as punishment. For comfort/status, try an available modest alternative; for food or sexual questions, preserve nourishment, freely revocable consent and appropriate individual guidance rather than inventing a quota.

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Decline or defer this purchase on its cost and purpose. Useful professional recognition can remain legitimate; the criterion is its actual role and tradeoff, not a universal ban on visibility.
